The pet shall disappear forever if you can't resurrect it within a certain amount of time. What is the maximum amount of time to resurrect a pet?

tutorials.7072:
So, you want to learn about the pets? Good, I will teach you everything.
First of all, I'll tell you about the wolves, since it is the first pet that you will breed. A wolf, is an animal whose sense of smell can reach an object as far as 2.4 km away. Also when they hunt, they have a habit of forming a pack of 7-14 with a male leader in front.
Concerning their appearance, a fully grown wolf won't necessarily be heavier than a grown-up man. The difference from a dog, which is a tamed animal, is that wolves always have their tail dangling down.
tutorials.7091:
We should talk about the wolf that you will be raising...
I must first explain their reproductive cycle. A wolf's fertility period is normally 1-2 months, and the pregnancy lasts for approximately 60-62 days . Normally, they will give birth to 3-6 cubs, but can produce up to 10 cubs at a time. They create a very safe home for their young ones. Places such as between rocks, under cliffs, and caves.
Wolves are more omnivirous than assumed. A full grown wolf can easily devour a calf or goat whole. Wolves also eat the flesh of dead animals, wild pheasants, and even berries. They can go without food for 5-6 days, but cannot live long without water.
tutorials.7256:
Pets can be very useful creatures.
If you are unable to carry items due to space or weight restrictions, you can transfer items to your pet and they will carry them for you. Bear in mind that they cannot run errands.
If your pet is killed it may be resurrected within 20 minutes. If it is not revived within the time limit, the pet will be gone forever.

Your pet shall be a wolf. You must learn more about them.
Wolves are biologically classified as canines. Canines are extremely varied, and include dogs, raccoons, foxes, jackals, and even timberwolves. The lifespan of wolves in the wild is unknown, but wolves in captivity can live from 12 to 15 years.
